chunks: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Warrāq, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated from Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the mute person: how does he swear an oath when a debt is claimed against him and the claimant has no evidence? He said: “Indeed, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was presented with a mute person against whom a debt was claimed. He denied it, and the claimant had no evidence against him. So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: ‘Praise belongs to Allah, who has not taken me out of the world until I have clarified for the community all that it needs.’”

Then he said: “Bring me a muṣḥaf.” It was brought to him. He said to the mute person: “What is this?” So he raised his head toward the sky and gestured that it was the Book of Allah. Then he said: “Bring me his guardian.” So they brought his brother to him, and he seated him beside himself. Then he said: “O Qanbar, bring me an inkpot and a tray.” He brought them both. Then he said to the mute person’s brother: “Tell your brother: this is between you and him; indeed it is ʿAlī.” So he conveyed that to him.

Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام wrote: “By Allah, other than Whom there is no god, Knower of the unseen and the seen, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful, the seeker, the prevailing, the one who harms, the one who benefits, the destroyer, the one who reaches, the one who knows the secret and the open—indeed so-and-so son of so-and-so, the claimant, has no right and no claim whatsoever against so-and-so son of so-and-so, meaning the mute person, in any way among the ways and for any cause among the causes.”
Then he washed it and ordered the mute person to drink it, but he refused, so he made the debt binding upon him.”

key_terms.الْأَخْرَسِ: the mute person who cannot verbally express the oath
key_terms.الْمُدَّعِيَ: the claimant bringing the legal accusation
key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ: legal proof or evidentiary support for a claim
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: a debt being claimed against someone
key_terms.مُصْحَفٍ: a written copy of the Qur'an used in the procedure
key_terms.يَحْلِفُ: to swear an oath in legal proceedings

ai.seo_question: How is a mute person made to swear an oath in an Islamic debt dispute when the claimant has no evidence?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a judicial ruling concerning how a mute person may be made to take an oath when a financial claim is brought against him without evidence. It presents a procedure attributed to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, showing both legal adjudication and the Imam’s clarification of practical rulings needed by the community.
